API reference¶

Flask application and routes¶

Single-page Flask analysis with one background scrape at a time.

class app.PullManager[source]¶
running()[source]¶
start()[source]¶
app.create_app(manager=None)[source]¶

The factory accepts an optional manager exposing running(), start(), state, and message. Route functions are nested inside the factory.

HTTP routes¶

Method and path

Response and behavior

GET / or /analysis

200 HTML with eleven answers. Query failures produce an error notice.

POST /pull-data

202 JSON {"ok": true} when accepted; 409 {"busy": true} when busy.

POST /update-analysis

200 refreshed HTML when idle; 409 {"busy": true} without querying when busy.

GET /pull-status

200 JSON with running, state, and message; 503 when the status check fails.

A 202 response acknowledges a job, not successful insertion. Check the progress endpoint for a later worker failure or completion.

Scraper¶

Module 2 scraper, adapted to fetch recent pages safely when requested.

scrape.scrape_data(known_ids=None, max_pages=10)[source]¶

Return cleaned recent records; cap each pull at ten sequential pages.

Stop after an entirely known page. A bounded pull can leave a large backlog; use the CLI with a larger max_pages value when collecting historical data.

Cleaner¶

clean_data accepts raw dictionaries and returns renamed fields. scrape_data in this module reads saved HTML, unlike the live scraper. save_data writes the cleaned JSON beside the cleaner script.

clean.clean_data(data_rows)[source]¶
clean.scrape_data()[source]¶
clean.save_data(records)[source]¶

Loader¶

normalize returns a tuple in COLUMNS order and raises ValueError for an unusable result URL. load_records returns integer counts named inserted, duplicates, and skipped. Malformed input records are counted as skipped; database errors propagate to the transaction owner.

Load the local Module 2 JSON into PostgreSQL; repeat loads are safe.

Queries¶

Supply a psycopg connection to the raw SQL function or a SQLAlchemy session to the ORM function to control connection lifetime. Omitting it opens a configured connection or session for the call.

All eleven analyses expressed as executable PostgreSQL SELECT statements.

query_data.run_queries(connection=None)[source]¶

All webpage reads and the six required repeat analyses use ORM expressions.

orm_queries.statements()[source]¶
orm_queries.run_queries(session=None)[source]¶

Formatting and configuration¶

format_result converts query tuples into display strings. Percentages have two decimals; missing values display N/A.

Question wording and presentation shared by console, PDF, and Flask.
